newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - June 13.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - June 13.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Friday and main factors likely to affect trading:
* Philippine shares will likely move in a tight band with an upward bias as gains will be limited by some players taking the day off after Thursday's holiday, traders said.

* Lippo Securities' Jidgette Valenzuela said Merrill Lynch's statement that it will reduce its weighting for Hong Kong in favor of South Korea and the Philippines will be positive for the local bourse and said foreign investors would gradually accumulate blue chips in the coming weeks.
* Manila's financial and equities markets were closed on Thursday due to the 99th Independence Day celebrations.
* On Wednesday, the Philippine composite index closed 12.63 points higher at 2,787.74 points.
* The Dow Jones on Thursday ended 135.64 points higher at 7,711.47. PLDT's ADR closed unchanged at $59 1/2.
* Merrill Lynch said it expects a 10-15 percent correction in Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index from recent highs and will reduce its weighting in Hong Kong in favour of South Korea and the Philippines.
* The Philippine peso closed lower on Wednesday at 26.378 to the dollar vs 26.373.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was unchanged at 14.03125 percent.
* The Central Bank reduced its benchmark overnight borrowing rate on Friday by one percentage point to 13.0 percent while the overnight lending rate was cut to 15.0 percent from 16.0.

* The Central Bank may restructure its $1.25 billion Yankee bond underwriting team after members gave conflicting advice on the timing and pricing of its long-delayed inaugural float, a Bank official said.

* Philippine Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero said he would review the administrative order which provided lower tariffs for selected imported farm products, two days after a Manila regional trial court issued a restraining order against the implementation of the new tariff scheme.

* Reynolds Philippines Corp said it planned to diversify and invest in petrochemical projects with BP Holdings International B.V., Sumitomo Corp and the Malaysian national oil firm Petroliam Nasional Berhad (Petronas).

* Manila Bulletin said that a further easing for the entry of telecommunication providers, particularly in the area of satellite service, was one of the proposals adopted during the recently concluded two-day multi-sectoral National Development Summit.
* Inquirer said MBF Holdings Berhad, a Malaysian conglomerate, is set to acquire 60 percent of Prime Savings Bank for 500 million pesos.
* Times Journal reported that San Miguel Corp recenltly opened a modern brewery in Indonesia with its partners PT Delta Djakarta in Bekasi Industrial Estate.

* The Philippine Star said quoting bank sources that Victorias Milling Co and its creditor banks are set to hold a crucial meeting today to thresh out the issue of unsecured refined sugar delivery orders.
